# flamelens

flamelens is an interactive flamegraph viewer for the terminal.

Description

flamelens reads folded stacks (stack traces aggregated in the "folded" format) and
renders an interactive flamegraph in a terminal UI so you can explore profiling data
without opening a browser.

Usage

Run flamelens with a folded stacks filename, or pipe folded stacks data to it:

flamelens <folded-stacks-filename>

or

cat folded-stacks.txt | flamelens

Live mode

flamelens can attach to a running process to display a live flamegraph (when supported):

flamelens --pid <pid-of-process>

Viewing perf data

You can generate folded stacks from perf and pipe them to flamelens, for example:

perf script -i perf.data | <tool-to-collapse-perf-output> | flamelens

Key bindings

- h/j/k/l or arrow keys: Navigate cursor for frame selection
- f: Scroll down
- b: Scroll up
- G: Scroll to bottom
- g: Scroll to top
- Enter: Zoom in on the selected frame
- Esc: Reset zoom
- /<regex>: Find and highlight frames matching the regex
- #: Find and highlight frames matching the selected frame
- n: Jump to next match
- N: Jump to previous match
- r: Reset to default view
- z (in Live mode): Freeze the flamegraph
- q (or Ctrl + c): Exit

Examples

- Open a folded stacks file:

  flamelens folded.txt

- Pipe collapsed perf output:

  perf script -i perf.data | inferno-collapse-perf | flamelens

Notes

This README intentionally omits build- and implementation-specific details.

    /// Profile data filename
    pub filename: Option<String>,

    /// Whether to sort the stacks by time spent
    #[arg(long)]
    pub sorted: bool,

    /// Print data to stdout on exit. Useful when piping to other tools
    #[arg(long)]
    pub echo: bool,

    /// Show debug info
    #[arg(long)]
    pub debug: bool,
}

    let args = Args::parse();

        (filename.clone(), data)
    } else {
        let mut buf = Vec::new();
        io::stdin()

            .expect("Could not read stdin");
        let data = String::from_utf8(buf).expect("Could not parse stdin");
        ("stdin".to_string(), data)
    };
    let _ = is_stdin;

    let mut app = app::App::new(name, &data, args.sorted, args.debug);
    let res = app.run();

        if !data.ends_with('\n') {
            println!();
        } else if !data.is_empty() {
            println!();
        } else {
            println!();
        }
    }
    res
}

    /// Return the indexes of the visible rows.
    ///
    /// The algorithm works as follows:
    /// - start at the offset and calculate the height of the rows that can be displayed within the
    ///   area.
    /// - if the selected row is not visible, scroll the table to ensure it is visible.
    /// - if there is still space to fill then there's a partial row at the end which should be
    ///   included in the view.
    fn visible_rows(&self, state: &TableState, area: Rect) -> (usize, usize) {
        let last_row = self.rows.len().saturating_sub(1);
        let mut start = state.offset.min(last_row);

        if let Some(selected) = state.selected {
            start = start.min(selected);
        }

        let mut end = start;
        let mut height = 0;

        for item in self.rows.iter().skip(start) {
            if height + item.height > area.height {
                break;
            }
            height += item.height_with_margin();
            end += 1;
        }

        if let Some(selected) = state.selected {
            let selected = selected.min(last_row);

            // scroll down until the selected row is visible
            while selected >= end {
                height = height.saturating_add(self.rows[end].height_with_margin());
                end += 1;
                while height > area.height {

                    start += 1;
                }
            }
        }

        // Include a partial row if there is space
        if height < area.height && end < self.rows.len() {
            end += 1;
        }

        (start, end)
    }

        let mut height_from_offset = 0;

fn truncate_to_width(s: &str, max_w: usize) -> String {
    if max_w == 0 {
        return String::new();
    }
    let mut out = String::new();
    let mut w = 0usize;
    for c in s.chars() {
        let cw = UnicodeWidthChar::width(c).unwrap_or(0);
        if w + cw > max_w {
            break;
        }
        out.push(c);
        w += cw;
    }
    out
}

def capture(exe, keys_seq, rows=24, cols=80):

    p=subprocess.Popen([exe,"/tmp/data.txt"], stdin=slave, stdout=slave, stderr=slave, close_fds=True)
    os.close(slave)
    fcntl.fcntl(master, fcntl.F_SETFL, os.O_NONBLOCK)
    frames=[]
    def drain(wait=0.55):
        data=b""; end=time.time()+wait
        while time.time()<end:
            r,_,_=select.select([master],[],[],0.05)
            if r:
                try:
                    c=os.read(master,65536)
                    if not c: break
                    data+=c
                except: break
        return data

    for k in keys_seq:

    os.write(master,b"q"); frames.append(drain(0.4))
    try: p.wait(timeout=1)
    except: p.kill()

fn render_line(wrapped: &WrappedLine<'_, '_>, area: Rect, buf: &mut Buffer, y: u16) {
    let mut x = get_line_offset(wrapped.width, area.width, wrapped.alignment);
    for StyledGrapheme { symbol, style } in wrapped.graphemes {
        let width = symbol.cell_width();
        if width == 0 {
            continue;
        }
        // Make sure to overwrite any previous character with a space (rather than a zero-width)
        let symbol = if symbol.is_empty() { " " } else { symbol };
        let position = Position::new(area.left() + x, area.top() + y);
        buf[position].set_symbol(symbol).set_style(*style);
        x += width;
    }
}

const fn get_line_offset(line_width: u16, text_area_width: u16, alignment: Alignment) -> u16 {
    match alignment {
        Alignment::Center => (text_area_width / 2).saturating_sub(line_width / 2),
        Alignment::Right => text_area_width.saturating_sub(line_width),
        Alignment::Left => 0,
    }
}

impl Styled for Paragraph<'_> {
    type Item = Self;

    fn style(&self) -> Style {
        self.style
    }

    fn set_style<S: Into<Style>>(self, style: S) -> Self::Item {
        self.style(style)
    }
}
